posts.title: 6 Signs Your Roof Has Hail Damage (and What to Do Next)
posts.excerpt: Hail damage is easy to miss from the ground. Here are the six signs we check first on Northwest Georgia roofs — and how the insurance process actually works.
posts.contentHtml:
[Fixture post — replaced automatically by the live WordPress feed at deploy time.]

Spring storms roll up the I-75 corridor every year, and most hail damage never shows up as a leak right away. Here is what our inspectors look for.

1. Bruised or dented shingles

Hail impact crushes the granule layer and leaves a soft spot underneath. From the ground it looks like nothing; on the roof it reads like a fingerprint.

2. Granules in your gutters

A sudden pile of granules in the downspout splash blocks after a storm usually means the protective layer of your shingles took a beating.

3. Dented vents, flashing, and gutters

Metal tells the truth. If the soft metals on your roof are dinged, the shingles took the same hits.

If any of this sounds like your roof, a free inspection takes about 30 minutes and you'll see photos of everything we find.

posts.title: Metal vs. Shingle Roofs in Georgia: An Honest Comparison
posts.excerpt: Metal roofs and architectural shingles both make sense in North Georgia — for different houses and budgets. Here's how we help homeowners choose.
posts.contentHtml:
[Fixture post — replaced automatically by the live WordPress feed at deploy time.]

We install both, so we don't have a horse in this race. The right answer depends on your roofline, your timeline in the home, and your budget.

Where shingles win

Upfront cost, easy repairs, and huge color selection. Modern architectural shingles handle our humidity well and look right on most subdivisions from Dalton to Cartersville.

Where metal wins

Lifespan and weather shrug-off. On cabins around Ellijay and farmhouses out in the county, standing seam sheds limbs, ice, and heavy rain for decades.

posts.title: Filing a Roof Insurance Claim in Georgia or Tennessee: A Homeowner's Guide
posts.excerpt: Storm damage claims aren't complicated once you know the order of operations. Here's the process we walk homeowners through every week.
posts.contentHtml:

The single biggest mistake homeowners make is calling the insurance company before they have documentation. Get the inspection and photo report first — then you're filing a claim with evidence instead of a guess.

The order of operations

  1. Free inspection and photo documentation
  2. Review the findings together
  3. File with your carrier
  4. Adjuster meeting — we're on the roof with them
  5. Scope agreement and scheduling
